formulaSheet.expression: Q_new(s,a) = Q_old(s,a) + η [r + γ max_a′ Q_old(s′,a′) − Q_old(s,a)]
assumptions: Read all right-hand-side Q values before the current write.
The numerical demonstrations use one sequential update.
For explicitly terminal transitions the demonstrations assume zero bootstrap; this is stated separately because p905 does not specify terminal-row initialization.
applications: Learning action values without a perfect transition/reward model.
commonMistakes: Replacing Q directly with the target when η is not one.
Omitting the subtraction of the old Q inside the TD error.
Confusing learning rate with discount factor.

formulaSheet.title: A* priority and heuristic

sourceRefs.locator: Main text and labeled figure on the inspected source page
sourceRefs.evidenceText:
3. A-Star
•  The A* (A-star) search algorithm is a widely used
   graph search technique in robot navigation that
   finds the optimal path between two points by
   using a heuristic to guide its search.

•  Mathematical Notation: Minimizes f(v)=g(v)+h(v),
   where:
   – g(v) is the path cost from the start to vertex v
      (cost-to-come).
   – h(v) is a heuristic estimating the distance from v
      to the goal (cost-to-go).



                                                                                                            32

sourceRefs.locator: Main text and labeled figure on the inspected source page
sourceRefs.evidenceText:
3. A-Star
•  The performance and accuracy of A* depend critically on the choice of the heuristic
   function:
➢Admissibility: A* is guaranteed to find the lowest-cost path only if the heuristic is
   "admissible," meaning it never overestimates the actual cost of reaching the goal.
  A non-admissible heuristic may lead to a non-optimal path.
➢Common heuristic function Examples:
   – Minimum-Distance: The Euclidean distance is a standard admissible heuristic
      because it is the shortest possible path between two
       points and cannot be an overestimate. (this example)
   – Minimum-Time: The heuristic must represent the travel
      time at the maximum possible speed in the
      environment to remain admissible.


                                                                                                            33

variables.f(v): estimated complete route cost through v

units.g,h,f: same cost units; kilometres in the road example

assumptions: For the minimum-cost guarantee, h must not overestimate the true remaining cost.
The runtime uses goal-on-pop, permits reopening, and requires h(goal)=0 for the stated guarantee.
Euclidean distance is an admissible lower bound when actual path costs represent compatible physical distances.
applications: Guide path search toward a goal.
For minimum time, use distance divided by a valid maximum speed as a lower-bound estimate.
commonMistakes: Adding a distance heuristic to a time cost without converting units.
Treating an arbitrary heuristic as automatically admissible.
Selecting by h alone, which is not A*.

sourceRefs.evidenceText:
Probability and Statistics – Bayesian estimation (Cont.)
•  Bayesian Updating
             •  Begin with an initial belief (prior)
             •  Each new sensor observation updates this belief
             •  The updated belief (posterior) becomes the new prior
•  Robot Sensor Example
   – A mobile robot estimates its distance to a wall using a noisy range sensor:
             •  MLE: estimates distance using only the latest measurements
             • MAP: combines new measurements with prior knowledge
                 (e.g., map information)
   – As more sensor data arrives, the robot’s estimate
      becomes more accurate and stable.
 •   Bayesian estimation allows robots to continuously refine sensor-
    based estimates by combining data with prior knowledge.

left.title: Prior
left.description: Belief before incorporating the current observation.

right.title: Posterior
right.description: Belief after updating with the observation; becomes the next prior.

confusionPairs.discriminatingRule: Ask whether the current evidence has already been incorporated.
confusionPairs.commonConfusion: Do not confuse posterior P(H|E) with likelihood P(E|H).

Step-by-Step Execution
•  Step 5: Expand cheapest node, E(7).

3. A-Star
•  The performance and accuracy of A* depend critically on the choice of the heuristic

➢Admissibility: A* is guaranteed to find the lowest-cost path only if the heuristic is
